slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Did Genesis predict when Jesus would come? Genesis says Judah will keep the royal sceptre “until Shiloh comes.” Some Christians treat this as a deadline for God’s promised ruler to arrive.
slides.body: Genesis says Judah will keep the royal sceptre “until Shiloh comes.” Some Christians treat this as a deadline for God’s promised ruler to arrive.
slides.heading: Did Genesis predict when Jesus would come?

slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Gen 49:10: The scepter will not depart from Judah, nor the staff from between his feet, until Shiloh comes and the allegiance of the nations is his.
slides.body: The scepter will not depart from Judah, nor the staff from between his feet, until Shiloh comes and the allegiance of the nations is his.
slides.heading: Gen 49:10

slides.alt_text: The claimed New Testament fulfilment in Gal 4:4, BSB: But when the time had fully come, God sent His Son, born of a woman, born under the law,
slides.body: But when the time had fully come, God sent His Son, born of a woman, born under the law,
slides.heading: Claimed fulfilment · Gal 4:4

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Why Christians connect them The verse can be read as promising a future ruler from Judah. Jesus is from Judah’s royal family, and Christians believe he arrived at God’s chosen time.
slides.body: The verse can be read as promising a future ruler from Judah. Jesus is from Judah’s royal family, and Christians believe he arrived at God’s chosen time.
slides.heading: Why Christians connect them

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: But there is no clear deadline Experts disagree about what “Shiloh” means, and the verse never defines when Judah loses the sceptre. The New Testament passages do not supply the missing date.
slides.body: Experts disagree about what “Shiloh” means, and the verse never defines when Judah loses the sceptre. The New Testament passages do not supply the missing date.
slides.heading: But there is no clear deadline

title: Does Genesis set a deadline for Jesus’s birth?
